Special Issue Deep Dive

Housing Affordability in District 24

With median home prices topping $450,000 and Danbury rents rising, housing costs are the #1 challenge facing working families, first-time buyers, and seniors. Here is how the candidates’ records and plans compare.

Historic 2025 Legislative Milestone • Landmark Housing Omnibus Act (HB 8002)

Julie Kushner’s Leadership on Building Affordable Housing

As Senate Deputy President Pro Tempore and Labor Committee Co-Chair, Senator Julie Kushner was the chief Senate architect and negotiator of Connecticut’s landmark 2025 Housing Omnibus Act (originally HB 8002)—unleashing over $350 million in state bonding for transit-oriented workforce housing, sewer infrastructure, and $50,000 first-time homebuyer grants.

Danbury Rail & Downtown Core

$15M+ Downtown Transit Housing

Directed over $15 million in dedicated state bonding and CIF funds to modernize Downtown Danbury's sewer and transit infrastructure, accelerating the conversion of vacant commercial parcels and surface lots near the Metro-North station into vibrant workforce housing with ground-floor retail.

✓ Unlocks 500+ downtown workforce units
Local Workforce Pipeline

Danbury Hospital & Teacher Housing

Established dedicated workforce preference allocations ensuring Danbury Hospital nurses, medical technicians, public school educators, and Western Connecticut State University (WCSU) faculty can afford to live in the community where they serve.

✓ Keeps essential municipal workers in Danbury
New Fairfield & Ridgefield

Suburban Planning & 8-30g Moratoriums

Provided direct state planning grants to New Fairfield and Ridgefield to craft town-tailored housing plans, expand gentle middle housing, and achieve statutory 8-30g moratoriums cooperatively without contentious builder lawsuits.

✓ Preserves local zoning authority
Environmental Protection

Candlewood Lake & Watershed Safeguards

Built in strict environmental review and water capacity safeguards protecting Candlewood Lake, Squantz Pond, Lake Kenosia, and local wetlands from inappropriate high-density runoff or septic overload.

✓ 100% CTLCV environmental compliance
First-Time Homebuyers

$50,000 Time To Own Down Payment Grants

Replenished Connecticut's signature 0% forgivable down payment assistance fund so local young families, nurses, firefighters, and municipal workers can afford to buy their first single-family home or condo in District 24.

✓ Turns renters into homeowners with immediate equity
Senior Homeowners

Senior Aging-in-Place & ADU Flexibility

Provided funding for accessible home retrofits (ramps, walk-in showers) and ADU permitting flexibility so longtime senior residents across District 24 can generate rental income or downsize without leaving their hometowns.

✓ Helps seniors stay in their family homes
How Julie Kushner Built the HB 8002 Coalition

Uniting Labor, Towns, and Environmental Champions

Senator Kushner utilized her position as Labor Committee Co-Chair and Deputy President Pro Tempore to bridge deep divides between urban centers and suburban towns. She ensured HB 8002 included prevailing wage standards for construction workers, guaranteed local municipal autonomy with state financial support, and defeated punitive top-down developer overrides.

"We cannot solve Connecticut's housing shortage with soundbites, obstruction, or by pitting towns against cities. HB 8002 delivers real state capital for sewer and transit infrastructure, gives our young workers $50,000 to buy their first home, and protects our lakes and local boards. That is what leadership delivers for Western Connecticut."
Challenger Melissa Lindsey's Stance

Opposed State Housing Funds & Demands 8-30g Repeal

Melissa Lindsey opposed HB 8002 and voted against state housing investments, claiming state funding for housing and transit constitutes 'government overreach.' Lindsey's platform focuses entirely on demanding the outright repeal of CGS § 8-30g without offering any replacement funding, infrastructure aid, or strategy to address skyrocketing home prices and rents in District 24.

District 24 Risk: Lindsey’s opposition to HB 8002 would forfeit over $15M in state infrastructure funds for Danbury and eliminate $50,000 homebuyer grants for local families.

First-Time Homebuyer Down Payment Assistance (HB 8002)

Forgivable down payment grants ($25K–$50K) vs. no homeownership aid

With median home prices exceeding $450,000 in Western Connecticut and interest rates elevated, saving for a 20% down payment is the single biggest barrier preventing young families, nurses, and teachers from owning a home in District 24.

Incumbent Record • HB 8002 Leader
Senator Julie Kushner
Democrat / Working Families • Deputy Senate President Pro Tempore

Housing Affordability2025

Landmark 2025 Connecticut Housing Omnibus Act (HB 8002)

Played a central Senate leadership role as Deputy President Pro Tempore in negotiating and passing Connecticut's historic 2025 Housing Omnibus Act (originally introduced as HB 8002). The landmark law delivered record state funding for transit-oriented workforce housing near downtown train corridors like Danbury, replenished the $50,000 Time To Own homebuyer grant fund, provided municipal infrastructure and sewer grants to encourage gentle housing growth, and enacted sweeping tenant protections against hidden rental junk fees and unfair evictions.

Spearheaded and passed landmark legislation providing up to 12 weeks of paid wage replacement for workers facing serious health conditions, caring for ill family members, or bonding with a newborn or adopted child. Challenger Platform Analysis

An Objective Review of Melissa Lindsey's Stated Platform

Examining the proposals, rhetoric, and practical district implications of the Republican challenger's 2026 campaign.

Campaign Pillar 1

"Affordability" & Utility Charges

Stated Position:

Advocates eliminating the "public benefits charge" on electric bills and opposes state climate fees on fossil fuel companies (HB 5156).

Policy Analysis & Tradeoffs:

While utility charges are a visible friction point, the public benefits charge finances energy efficiency audits, low-income heating assistance, and solar incentives. Cutting these charges without replacement revenue would shift costs directly onto municipal budgets. Meanwhile, Lindsey offers no framework for income tax reductions or property tax offsets.

Campaign Pillar 2

"Constitutional Freedoms" & Vaccines

Stated Position:

Focuses on "Medical Autonomy" and "Religious Liberty," advocating to restore religious exemptions for school vaccines and opposing state public health standards.

Policy Analysis & Tradeoffs:

Lindsey adopts slogans like "My Body, My Choice" solely in the context of resisting immunization requirements, while noticeably declining to support reproductive freedom, abortion access, or safe harbor protections for Connecticut women and healthcare providers.

Campaign Pillar 3

"Parental Rights" & School Vouchers

Stated Position:

Explicitly states on her campaign site: "How and where children are educated — I support school choice."

Policy Analysis & Tradeoffs:

Voucher / school choice programs siphon essential public tax dollars out of Danbury and New Fairfield public classrooms and redirect them to private academies. In contrast, Senator Kushner secured a historic 80% state reimbursement rate for the $164M Danbury Career Academy to strengthen local public education.

Campaign Pillar 4

"Public Safety" & Firearms

Stated Position:

Supports the right to bear arms, opposes creating new gun regulations, and emphasizes reversing police accountability legislation.

Policy Analysis & Tradeoffs:

Connecticut's evidence-based gun safety statutes (banning untraceable ghost guns, safe storage, and red flag laws) have made Connecticut one of the safest states in America. Opposing sensible gun safety measures runs contrary to the public safety interests of suburban and urban communities across District 24.

The Core Choice for Voters in 2026

While Melissa Lindsey offers standard challenger critiques regarding Hartford bureaucracy, Senator Julie Kushner has consistently used her seniority and majority leadership to deliver tangible legislative victories: paid family leave, insulin price caps, 100% senior retirement tax relief, and record school construction funds.
